Iowa property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • A property owner or aggrieved taxpayer may file a protest with the board of review on or after April 2 through April 30 of the assessment year. (Iowa Code 441.37; source)
  • Protest grounds: assessment not equitable compared with like property; assessed for more than authorized value; property not assessable, exempt or misclassified; error in assessment; fraud or misconduct (specifically stated). (Iowa Code 441.37; source)
  • Board of review decisions may be appealed to the Property Assessment Appeal Board within 20 days after the local board adjourns or May 31, whichever is later. (Iowa Code 441.37A; source)
  • The taxpayer may bypass PAAB and appeal the board of review decision directly to district court. (Iowa Code 441.37A; source)
  • District court appeal is filed with the clerk of district court within 20 days after the board's adjournment or May 31, whichever is later; the court hears it in equity with no presumption the assessment is correct. (Iowa Code 441.38; source)
  • Taxes on an assessment under appeal are not delayed; if reduced, taxes on the reduced portion are abated, refunded or credited. (Iowa Code 441.37A; source)
  • Property is valued at actual value and, except as otherwise provided, assessed at 100 percent of actual value. (Iowa Code 441.21; source)
  • The county treasurer offers delinquent parcels at public sale annually on the third Monday in June. (Iowa Code 446.7; source)
  • Redemption requires payment of the sale amount plus interest of two percent per month, each fraction counted as a full month. (Iowa Code 447.1; source)

title: Iowa Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home
content:
Iowa Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa

  • Iowa Homestead Exemption: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the Iowa Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • SF 2472 (2026 Iowa Acts), signed May 18, 2026, replaces the homestead tax credit with a homestead exemption of 10% of the taxable value of the homestead. (Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption | Department of Revenue; source)
  • The change is retroactive to assessment year 2026, applying to property taxes paid September 2027 and March 2028. (Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption | Department of Revenue; source)
  • Minimum exemption is $5,500 of taxable value; maximum is $20,000 of taxable value; the maximum is adjusted for inflation beginning assessment year 2027. (Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption | Department of Revenue; source)
  • Claimants age 65 or older on or before January 1 of the assessment year qualify for an additional exemption of $6,500 of taxable value, applied in successive years without refiling. (Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption | Department of Revenue; source)
  • Claimants who received the homestead credit or exemption before July 1, 2026 are automatically awarded the 10% exemption without refiling if still eligible. (Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption | Department of Revenue; source)
  • The disabled veteran homestead tax credit is not eliminated by this change. (Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption | Department of Revenue; source)
Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What changed with the Iowa homestead benefit in 2026?

Iowa swapped its homestead tax credit for a homestead exemption equal to 10 percent of the home's taxable value. Senate File 2472, signed May 18, 2026, made the change, according to the Iowa Department of Revenue.

The Department explains the difference this way: an exemption cuts the value you are taxed on, while a credit cuts the tax bill directly. The old credit equaled the levy on the first $4,850 of a home's value, with a floor of $62.50, under Iowa Code 425.1.

The change reaches back to assessment year 2026. It shows up on the property taxes paid in September 2027 and March 2028.

How much is the Iowa homestead exemption worth?

The exemption is 10 percent of taxable value, with a minimum of $5,500 and a maximum of $20,000 of taxable value. Starting with assessment years that begin on or after January 1, 2027, the $20,000 maximum is adjusted for inflation.

FeatureDetail
Rate10 percent of taxable value
Minimum exemption$5,500 of taxable value
Maximum exemption$20,000 of taxable value in 2026, indexed from 2027
Extra for age 65 and older$6,500 of taxable value
First applies toAssessment year 2026

Here is how the floor and cap play out. A house with a taxable value of $40,000 would get $5,500 instead of $4,000. A house with a taxable value of $250,000 would get $20,000 instead of $25,000. Those figures are illustrations of the rule, not quotes from any county.

The benefit is a reduction in taxable value, so the dollars saved depend on your local levy.

Who qualifies for the Iowa homestead exemption?

The owner must live in Iowa and occupy the home. County assessors describe the test as living there on July 1 and for at least six months of every year. The extra exemption for older owners requires the owner to be 65 or older on January 1 of the year of the application, per the Des Moines County assessor.

Other points that affect eligibility:

  • Owners who were already getting the credit before July 1, 2026 are awarded the 10 percent exemption automatically if they still qualify.
  • Owners 65 or older who qualify for the additional exemption do not have to refile each year.
  • The disabled veteran homestead credit remains in place and was not eliminated by the new law.

Iowa also has a military exemption for qualifying veterans, Guard members and reservists, and a family farm credit for tracts of 10 acres or more that are farmed by the owner or immediate family. Each has its own filing rules at the assessor's office.

How and when do I file for the homestead exemption?

Applications are due on or before July 1 of the year the exemption is first claimed. The form is Homestead Tax Exemption 54-028, linked from the Department of Revenue page, and it goes to your county assessor.

You only need to file once. The Des Moines County assessor says the exemption continues until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies. The family farm credit has a different date, November 1.

If you bought the house this spring, ask the assessor about the July 1 date before it passes.

How much land counts toward an Iowa homestead?

The home itself plus up to one-half acre inside a city plat or up to forty acres outside one. The Department of Revenue set this out in a June 2026 notice to assessors and auditors.

When a parcel has more land than the limit, the land value is scaled down before the exemption is figured. The notice gives an example of a two-acre parcel inside a city plat: its $10,000 land value is cut to $2,500 for homestead purposes.

The disabled veteran credit is narrower. For applications submitted on or after July 1, 2026, it covers the dwelling without appurtenances plus one-half acre, whether or not the land is in a plat.

Sellers of rural Iowa houses should look at this closely. A house on an 80-acre parcel is not fully covered, so the tax bill on the whole parcel can look different from a town lot.

What happens to the homestead exemption when you sell the house?

It ends with the sale. The assessor's rule is that the exemption lasts until the property is sold or the owner stops qualifying, and the buyer files for their own.

That has a few practical effects at closing:

  • Property tax for the sale year is still billed in two installments, delinquent after September 30 and March 31 under Iowa Code 445.37.
  • The seller's share of the current installment is normally settled between buyer and seller through the closing statement.
  • Moving out before July 1 can affect whether you meet the occupancy test for that year.

If you are selling because you cannot keep up with taxes or repairs, a cash sale can shorten the time you carry the house. Our Iowa property tax guide covers appeals and what happens when taxes go unpaid.

What other 2026 Iowa property tax changes affect home sellers?

Several rules changed alongside the exemption. The Iowa League of Cities summary of SF 2472 lists the following.

  • The residential rollback for fiscal year 2027 is 44.5345 percent.
  • Homes with three or more dwelling units move into a restored multi-residential class on January 1, 2027. Duplexes and single-family homes stay residential.
  • Property is generally assessed every two years.
  • Starting January 1, 2027, the burden of proof shifts to the assessor when an assessment increases by more than 10 percent.
  • State funding for the old credit phases out between July 1, 2027 and July 1, 2029.

A property tax protest is filed with the local board of review from April 2 through April 30, under Iowa Code 441.37. In a county under a disaster declaration, the window moves to May 1 through June 5.

Which new Iowa laws change how a house sale works?

Two Iowa laws that took effect July 1, 2026 touch ordinary home sales. Iowa Realtors summarized them in its overview of new laws.

  • Under SF 2448, homeowners associations must certify whether dues are current and disclose approved upcoming assessments and transfer-related fees.
  • After a buyer asks for repairs based on an inspection, the seller can request the matching sections of the report. If they are not supplied, the seller may cancel the contract without penalty.
  • Under SF 2472, a new FirstHome Iowa savings account lets first-time buyers set money aside for down payments and closing costs.

These rules mostly matter to sellers who list with an agent and negotiate repairs. A direct as-is sale skips the repair-request step.

More questions about Iowa Homestead Exemption

How much is the Iowa homestead exemption?

It is 10 percent of your home's taxable value, no less than $5,500 and no more than $20,000 for assessment year 2026. The cap is adjusted for inflation starting with assessment years that begin in 2027.

Do I need to reapply if I already get the Iowa homestead credit?

No. Owners who received the homestead credit or exemption before July 1, 2026 are automatically awarded the 10 percent exemption if they are still eligible.

What is the deadline to claim the Iowa homestead exemption?

July 1 of the year you first claim it. You file Form 54-028 with your county assessor.

Does the homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. It continues only until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies, so the new owner must apply on their own.

How much extra do homeowners age 65 and older get?

An additional $6,500 of taxable value. You must be 65 or older by January 1 of the assessment year, and you do not refile in later years.

Is the disabled veteran credit gone?

No. The Department of Revenue says the disabled veteran homestead tax credit is not eliminated by SF 2472. For applications on or after July 1, 2026, it covers the dwelling plus one-half acre.

title: Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Iowa inheritance tax is not applicable for deaths occurring on or after 1/1/25. (Introduction to Iowa Inheritance Tax | Department of Revenue; source)
  • Iowa estate tax is not applicable for deaths on or after 1/1/05. (Introduction to Iowa Inheritance Tax | Department of Revenue; source)
  • For earlier deaths, the inheritance tax return was due by the last day of the ninth month after death and the beneficiary was responsible for the tax. (Introduction to Iowa Inheritance Tax | Department of Revenue; source)
Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Iowa have an estate tax or an inheritance tax today?

Iowa has neither one for a person who dies now. The state estate tax stopped applying to deaths on or after January 1, 2005, and the inheritance tax stopped applying to deaths on or after January 1, 2025, according to the Iowa Department of Revenue.

The two taxes work differently, and heirs often mix them up. An estate tax is charged on the whole estate. Iowa's inheritance tax was based on what each beneficiary had a right to receive, which is why the rate depended on who the heir was.

For anyone who inherits an Iowa house now, the practical result is simple: no Iowa death tax return stands between the heirs and a sale. Other costs still apply, and the sections below cover them.

How was the Iowa inheritance tax phased out?

The Legislature cut the tax in steps over four years and then ended it. Under Iowa Code 450.10(7), the normal rates were reduced by a set percentage depending on the year of death.

Year of deathRate reduction
202120 percent
202240 percent
202360 percent
202480 percent
2025 and laterChapter does not apply

The end point is written into chapter 450, which says it does not apply to property of estates of decedents dying on or after January 1, 2025. The tax on unknown heirs was cut on the same schedule and ended for 2025 deaths too.

If the person who owned the house died in 2024 or earlier, the old rules can still matter, so keep reading.

Who paid inheritance tax before 2025, and who was exempt?

Close family paid nothing. Property passing to a surviving spouse, parents and grandparents, children, stepchildren, grandchildren and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450.

Everyone else could owe tax, and the rate climbed with the amount received. The statute set these brackets before the phase-down reductions:

  • Siblings, sons-in-law and daughters-in-law: 5 percent on the first $12,500, rising by bracket to 10 percent on amounts above $150,000.
  • Other heirs, such as nieces, nephews, cousins and friends: 10 percent up to $50,000, 12 percent to $100,000 and 15 percent above that.
  • Out-of-state charitable bodies: 10 percent on the full amount.
  • For-profit firms and corporations: 15 percent on the full amount.

Some transfers were left out altogether. An estate of $25,000 or less after debts owed no tax, tangible personal property was exempt when the total was $5,000 or less, and gifts to qualifying charitable, educational and religious groups were excluded.

What deadlines applied to an Iowa inheritance tax return?

The tax came due on the last day of the ninth month after the date of death, and the return was due the same day unless none was required. The Department's own page says the beneficiary was responsible for the tax on earlier deaths.

The Department of Revenue could extend payment for up to ten years from the end of the month of death to avoid hardship, but interest ran from the original date. Late payment also carried a penalty.

These dates only matter now for an older death. A house inherited from someone who died in, say, 2023 can still carry an open file, which is worth checking before closing.

Can an old inheritance tax lien still affect selling an inherited Iowa house?

It can, for deaths before 2025. Under Iowa Code 450.7, the tax was a lien on the taxable estate and the decedent's property from the date of death until paid, and a sale did not wipe it out.

The same section says the lien generally ends ten years after death, and it ranks ahead of later mortgages, buyers and judgment creditors without any recorded notice. Property passing to a spouse, parents, children and other lineal descendants was never subject to the lien.

Ways the lien was released or cleared:

  • Filing a receipt showing the tax was paid with the clerk of court.
  • Filing a certificate that no tax was owed.
  • Filing a release or waiver.
  • Where no return was required, filing an affidavit describing the real estate in the county where it sits (section 450.22).

A title company or estate attorney normally handles this paperwork. If you are an heir selling a house from a pre-2025 death, ask them whether anything is still open of record.

Does the federal estate tax reach an Iowa house?

Only for very large estates. The IRS lists a filing threshold of $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026 and $13,990,000 for 2025, as shown on its estate tax page.

An estate must file a federal return when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, goes above that figure. A surviving spouse can also elect to carry over the unused exemption of the person who died. That election is made on a timely filed estate tax return.

Most Iowa families who inherit a house will fall far below the threshold. The house is one asset among others in that total, and a sale price does not by itself trigger a filing.

What property taxes still follow an inherited Iowa home?

Ordinary property tax continues whether or not anyone owes a death tax. Iowa counties bill in two installments, and the first becomes delinquent on October 1 and the second on April 1, under Iowa Code 445.37. If the last day of September or March falls on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month.

Heirs sometimes assume the homestead benefit passes along with the house. It does not run on its own. The Des Moines County assessor explains that once a person qualifies, the exemption continues until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies, so an heir who will not live there may be taxed without it. Our Iowa homestead exemption guide covers the 2026 change.

Plan for the taxes due on the estate's calendar. A cash buyer can usually close ahead of an installment date, and the settlement figures show what is paid from proceeds.

What does selling an inherited house in Iowa involve now?

The steps depend on how title is held and on whether a court-supervised estate is open. If the owner died with a will or without one, the person with authority over the estate signs the deed, and the buyer's title company will ask for proof of that authority.

Recording the deed also triggers the Iowa transfer tax, set by Iowa Code 428A.1 at eighty cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. It is paid to the county recorder, and a declaration of value goes in with the deed. Transfers with no consideration are not taxed.

  • Gather the death certificate and any will.
  • Confirm who has authority to sell, whether an executor or heirs holding title.
  • Ask the title company to search for liens, including any pre-2025 inheritance tax lien.
  • Check which property tax installment is next.

We buy inherited Iowa houses as they stand, which helps when the home needs repairs the heirs would rather not fund.

More questions about Iowa Estate and Inheritance Tax

Is there an inheritance tax in Iowa in 2026?

No. Iowa's Department of Revenue states that the inheritance tax does not apply to deaths occurring on or after January 1, 2025, so a 2026 death creates no Iowa inheritance tax return.

Does Iowa have a state estate tax?

No. The Iowa estate tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2005. The federal estate tax is separate and has a 2026 filing threshold of $15,000,000.

Do I owe Iowa inheritance tax if my parent died in 2024?

A child inheriting from a parent owed nothing, because property passing to children and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450. Siblings and other heirs could owe a tax at rates reduced by 80 percent for 2024 deaths.

Can an inheritance tax lien block a sale of the house?

It can for older deaths. The lien under section 450.7 generally ends ten years after death, but it can be released earlier by a receipt, certificate or waiver, and a title company can tell you whether one is on record.

Who pays the Iowa transfer tax when an inherited house is sold?

The statute sets the amount and says it is paid to the county recorder, but the text we reviewed does not say which party bears it. Settle that point in the purchase contract with your title company.

Do heirs keep the homestead exemption on an inherited Iowa house?

Not automatically. County assessors say the exemption continues only while the owner still qualifies, and it ends when the property is sold.

This guide covers Iowa foreclosure sales according to official sources.

What the official sources say

  • The officer must give four weeks' notice of the time and place of sale of real property. (Iowa Code 626.74; source)
  • Notice is posted in at least three public places in the county including the courthouse, plus two weekly newspaper publications for real estate, the first at least four weeks before sale. (Iowa Code 626.75; source)
  • Judgments for money or possession are enforced by execution. (Iowa Code 626.1; source)
  • After sale the debtor may redeem within one year and keeps possession meanwhile. (Iowa Code 628.3; source)
  • A defendant who stays in possession after foreclosure or execution sale is subject to forcible entry and detainer. (Iowa Code 648.1; source)
  • Iowa mortgages and deeds of trust may be foreclosed only by court action in equity, except under the alternative procedure of section 654.18. (Iowa Code 654.1; source)
  • Alternative nonjudicial voluntary foreclosure requires mutual written agreement; the mortgagor conveys all interest to the mortgagee and the mortgagee waives any deficiency. (Iowa Code 654.18; source)
  • Junior lienholders get 30 days from mailing of notice to exercise redemption rights under the voluntary procedure; mortgagor has a five-business-day cancellation right. (Iowa Code 654.18; source)
  • After a foreclosure sale the debtor may redeem within one year from the day of sale and keeps possession meanwhile; the first six months is exclusive to the debtor. (Iowa Code 628.3; source)
  • For mortgaged property under 10 acres, the mortgage may reduce the redemption period to six months (three months if not agricultural) if the mortgagee waives any deficiency. (Iowa Code 628.26; source)
  • Creditors may redeem within nine months from the day of sale if the debtor does not redeem. (Iowa Code 628.5; source)
  • For agricultural land, a creditor may not start foreclosure until it gives a notice of right to cure and waits 45 days. (Iowa Code 654.2A; source)

title: Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House
content:
Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Cash Home Buyers in Iowa
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House sale
  • Turn the Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Iowa House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Iowa individual income tax is a flat 3.8 percent for 2026. (IDR Announces 2026 Individual Income Tax and Interest Rates; source)
Selling in Iowa?
We buy Iowa houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Iowa have a separate capital gains tax on a house sale?

No. Iowa does not charge a stand-alone capital gains tax. The profit from selling a house is reported as part of your Iowa individual income tax return, and for tax year 2026 the Department of Revenue says one flat rate of 3.8 percent applies to all levels of taxable income.

On the Iowa return, the capital gain or loss line starts with 100 percent of the amount from your federal Form 1040. The state says the capital gain deduction is not taken on that line, because a qualifying deduction goes on a separate line. If your federal return needs Schedule D and Form 8949, a copy goes with the Iowa return.

One note to avoid confusion: the 3.8 percent Iowa rate and the 3.8 percent federal net investment income tax share a number and nothing else. They are separate taxes with separate rules, and both can matter on a large gain.

How much gain on your Iowa home can you exclude?

If the house was your main home, you can generally exclude up to $250,000 of gain, or up to $500,000 on a joint return. Iowa says it generally follows the federal rules on excluding gain from a principal residence, so the federal exclusion also keeps that gain off your Iowa taxable income.

The IRS sets two tests, and you must meet both:

  • Ownership: you or your spouse owned the home for at least 24 months of the five years before the sale.
  • Use: you, and your spouse if filing jointly, each lived in it as a main home for at least 24 months of that same five-year period.

The two 24-month periods do not need to be the same months. Generally you cannot use the exclusion if you excluded gain from another home sale during the two years before this one. The IRS points to Publication 523 for exceptions and partial exclusions.

You must report the sale if you receive a Form 1099-S, even if the full gain is excludable, and if you cannot exclude all of the gain. Use Form 8949 with Schedule D.

What happens if the gain is larger than the exclusion?

Gain above the exclusion is taxed federally as a capital gain and in Iowa at the flat state rate. The federal rate depends on how long you held the property.

ItemRule from the source
Held one year or lessShort-term, taxed as ordinary income
Held more than one yearLong-term, federal rates of 0, 15 or 20 percent by taxable income
Unrecaptured section 1250 gain (depreciation on real property)Maximum federal rate of 25 percent
Iowa individual income tax, 20263.8 percent flat
Iowa interest on overdue tax, from January 1, 202610 percent a year, 0.8 percent a month

The federal net investment income tax is 3.8 percent for single filers above $200,000, joint filers above $250,000 and separate filers above $125,000 of modified adjusted gross income. The IRS says the tax does not apply to the part of a home sale gain that is excluded as a principal residence. Gain above the exclusion can be hit.

Which Iowa capital gain deductions were repealed?

Most Iowa capital gain deductions ended with tax year 2023. The Department of Revenue states that the repealed categories include gains from selling real estate used in a non-farm business, an entire business, timber, cattle, horses or breeding livestock (with an exception for retired farmers), and employer securities sold to a qualified Iowa employee stock ownership plan.

The change took effect January 1, 2023. Installment sales that began before that date still qualify for the deduction. The Department's deduction page still carries reference material for non-farm real property, but the state's 2023 changes page controls, and the statute governs in any dispute.

That matters to anyone who read older guidance that gave a ten-year holding rule for business real estate. If you sold rental or commercial property after 2022, do not rely on it.

  • Retired farmers aged 55 or older may still deduct gain from farm real estate if they materially participated in farming for ten years in total.
  • A retired farmer has a single lifetime election.
  • Electing the deduction blocks the beginning farmer tax credit and the farm lease income exclusion.
  • Gain from an employee-owned corporation's stock has its own phase-in: 33 percent excluded for 2023, 66 percent for 2024 and 100 percent from 2025.

A house in town or a rental house is not covered by those farm rules. A principal residence relies on the federal exclusion instead.

How does an inherited Iowa house change the gain?

Inherited property generally takes a new tax basis equal to its fair market value on the date of the owner's death, not the price the deceased originally paid. A sale soon after inheritance often produces little or no taxable gain for that reason.

The estate's personal representative can instead elect an alternate valuation date, which uses the value on that date. If you did not receive a Schedule A (Form 8971), the IRS says you can use the appraised value at death for state inheritance or transmission tax purposes. Property given to the decedent within one year before death can carry the decedent's adjusted basis rather than the death-date value.

Keep an appraisal from the date of death. It is the first document a tax preparer will ask for if you sell a house you inherited in Iowa, and it is hard to recreate later.

Do nonresidents owe Iowa tax on a house they sell in Iowa?

Yes, if the Iowa-source income reaches the filing trigger. The Department of Revenue lists capital gain on the sale of Iowa property, along with rental income, as income from Iowa property. A nonresident or part-year resident must file when Iowa-source net income is $1,000 or more, unless income falls under the standard thresholds.

For the 2025 return year those thresholds were more than $9,000 for single or married filing separately filers, and more than $13,500 for joint filers, head of household and qualifying surviving spouse. Higher amounts apply to people 65 and older.

People who sell an Iowa house after moving away, or heirs living out of state, often miss this step. Check it before the money is spent.

What other Iowa costs show up when a house is sold?

Iowa property tax and state transfer tax are separate from any income tax on the gain. Real estate transfer tax applies to a deed that conveys Iowa real estate when the consideration exceeds $500, at 80 cents for each $500 or fractional part above $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. The code treats the full price as consideration, including any lien the buyer assumes.

  • A declaration of value, signed by at least one buyer or seller, goes to the county recorder with the deed.
  • Personal property is presumed part of the price unless its value is stated on the instrument.
  • Property tax on Iowa homes runs a year behind and is billed in September and March.
  • A seller closing from July 1 to December 31 owes the September installment, and one closing from January 1 to June 30 owes the March one.

An as-is cash sale does not change these rules. It changes who pays for repairs and how fast the deal closes.

More questions about Iowa Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Is there a capital gains tax in Iowa?

Iowa has no separate capital gains tax. Gains are part of Iowa taxable income, which is taxed at a flat 3.8 percent for tax year 2026.

Do I pay Iowa tax on the sale of my primary residence?

Only on gain above the exclusion. Iowa generally follows the federal rule that lets you exclude up to $250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return, if you meet the ownership and use tests.

Can I deduct capital gains on a rental house sold in Iowa?

Not under the old non-farm real property deduction. The Department of Revenue says that deduction was repealed for tax years starting January 1, 2023, apart from installment sales begun before then.

Does Iowa tax gain when I inherit and sell a house?

Gain is measured from the stepped-up basis, usually the fair market value at the date of death. If you sell at about that value, little gain results.
